items.title: design(atlas): cold-tier shard format and restore path (#6042)
items.body: ## What The design doc for #6042 (task 13011): the cold-tier shard format and restore path, at `doc/2026-11-10T20-06-24Z_design_atlas_cold_tier_shard_format/`. It fixes what the #6026 versioning/retention design (§6) explicitly left to #6042: - **Container layout** — one immutable rustfs object: header, JSON manifest, span section (optionally zstd), uncompressed f32 vector section, checksum footer (SHA-256 per section + manifest). Byte-level layout specified; no libSQL-only assumptions. - **Manifest schema** — corpus/tier, source marks, per-version entries with lineage summaries (the #6026 §2.2 edge vocabulary) and occurrence lists, span table, vector model + dimensions (768 for the current corpus model), creation time, retention state at pack time, provenance. - **Packing rules** — one corpus + one class per shard, ~512 MiB target / 2 GiB ceiling, lineage grouping, whole versions only, idempotent re-pack. - **Fan-out contract** — cold shards are outside the default fan-out set; reached only by explicit version addressing (pin / `as_of`) or shard-addressed search, via a hot-side cold catalog. - **Restore / re-import procedure** — checksum-verified, provenance-additive, idempotent re-import under the version's original `(file_id, version_seq)` identity; model-mismatch flagging instead of silent mixing. - **Acceptance shape** — the named check `cold-roundtrip-verify`: hot → cold → hot with byte-identical spans and bit-identical vectors. - **Boundaries** — cold-before-delete and one-full-cycle-in-cold invariants against the #6041 retention engine (whose policy this doc does not duplicate); the #6043 PITR layer boundary taken as given (PITR is database disaster recovery, not corpus retention). Cold-eligibility starting defaults per class in §9. Implementation is split into follow-on issues in §10 of the doc (writer, restore importer, cold catalog + fan-out addressing, round-trip verifier, shard compaction); this PR lands the design only. ## Verification Readback checks from the task packet: the doc names every manifest field in #6042's scope (grep-verified); it states PITR is not a corpus-retention mechanism and defers the retention engine to #6041 (grep-verified); consistency read against the #6026 design and the #6043 decision record. Refs #6042 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: docs(atlas): content versioning + retention design (#6026)
items.body: Fixes #6026 ## What The Atlas content versioning + retention design doc — #6026's "Done looks like" — at `doc/2026-11-08T10-26-00Z_design_atlas_content_versioning_retention/`: - **Version object model** (§2): `file_id` vs `(file_id, version_seq)` identity (paths are version attributes, never identity), immutable versions, content stored once by hash, lineage edges (`edit` / `rename` / `split` / `merge` / `tombstone`) as first-class evidence-carrying rows, and chunks bound to versions by **occurrence** — so retention can never orphan a chunk a surviving version still points at. - **Lineage rules per source type** (§3): Atlas computes and stores its own edges. Git records no renames (per-diff `-M50%` heuristic re-guess), so git's output is one ingestion signal among several (segment/shared-chunk scoring, basename priors); rename-only commit hygiene is a hint-quality lever, not a correctness requirement. Non-git sources anchor on source-native ids or content-neighbourhood inference. - **Retention** (§4): per-class table (code / docs / session logs / chat logs / generated reports) with the three triggers parameterized per class — **by date, by increments, by access** (the access trigger consumes the per-version surfaced record from the #6018 stats/feedback design). Governed by the #3125 reconciliation: default keep; a version retires only when a trigger fires **and** its class rule permits; retirement is report-first (dry-run, #6041) and leaves a tombstone record. - **Cold rollout** (§6): hot → cold (rustfs) preserves resolvability — cold is a latency class, not a visibility class; deletion is the only hard end. PITR boundary kept per PR #6269: Turso PITR is whole-DB disaster recovery, never a retention mechanism. - **Query-side contract** (§5): newest-resolution as a query-time **view** (never destructive replace), tombstone heads do not resurface the previous version, `version` pinning and `as_of` parameters (with #5774/#5755), one-file-best-version hit grouping, and full-version logging per run feeding the query-trace design (#6027). - **Implementation split** (§8): storage/lineage and the query contract as new follow-ons under #6018; the retention engine and cold tier fold in the already-filed #6041 and #6042 rather than duplicating them. Design only; no implementation is authorized by the doc. Inputs are the settled ones from task 12445's triage verdict on #6026 — nothing re-litigated. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: doc(atlas): storage growth model + calibration of v1 retention defaults (#6061)
items.body: Design record for #6061: the Atlas storage growth model (per-source churn x retained versions, marginal bytes via the #6028 span-reuse ratio, hot/cold split, staging modelled separately) projected against the #6019 plan envelope, plus the calibration procedure that turns #6058 ingest-ledger data into per-class retention defaults for the #6026 / #6041 rule engine. Acceptance mapping (task 13013 packet): - Dated design record in doc/ with a doc/README.md index entry; inputs (churn, reuse ratio, retained-version counts, manifest/metadata, index amplification, hot vs cold) and the envelope projection are in sections 2-4, with a worked example. - Calibration procedure in section 5: the #6058 ledger fields consumed, weekly-then-monthly cadence, conservative (keep-more) v1 defaults, and cold-tier moves preceding deletions by at least one full retention cycle. - Inputs/outputs consumed from #6026/#6041 and #6028 are named explicitly (sections 3 and 5.3) rather than re-defined; the #6043 trigger-plus-class-rule requirement is honoured in section 6. - No destructive retention action is enabled by this design (section 6). Refs #6061. Design only; implementation follow-ons are listed in section 7 of the record. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

items.title: design(atlas): retention rule engine — schema, cadence, dry-run report, promotion path (#6041)
items.body: ## Summary The design record for #6041: the Atlas retention rule engine that parameterizes the parent policy in `doc/2026-11-08T10-26-00Z_design_atlas_content_versioning_retention/` (#6026, §4). Task 10569's triage verified the deliverable — rule schema, evaluation cadence, dry-run report format, promotion path — had never been produced; this record produces it, grounded strictly in the parent's §4.1 governing rule, §4.2 defaults, §4.3 triggers, §4.4 report-before-deletion, and §7 parameter boundary. Highlights: - **Schema as data:** one versioned rule record per (class, tier) with the §4.2 table as the initial rule set (all rows `dry-run`); trigger OR-combination and the §4.1 conjunction are fixed semantics, not per-rule options. - **Invariants made unrepresentable:** class rules mechanically checked to only narrow vs the default row; keep-newest-N floor and head protection applied after trigger evaluation; cold-before-delete per version (≥1 full cycle cold-tiered). - **Cadence:** weekly deterministic batch runs pinned to (lineage snapshot, surfaced-events snapshot, rule-set version) so any report re-derives byte-for-byte; on-demand dry-runs never count toward promotion. - **Promotion per rule:** dry-run → live-cold after two unchanged scheduled cycles, → live-delete after one further live-cold cycle, each step recorded by the row's override owner naming the earning run ids; any threshold edit resets the rule to dry-run; demotion is immediate. - **Report format:** JSON + human summary from the same data — per-rule candidates split would-cold-tier vs would-delete, grouped by trigger, with explicit protection notes and cycle-over-cycle deltas; deletion runs append their tombstone annex under the same run id. - **Governance:** the #3125 keep-ALL reconciliation is encoded per tier/class as §4.1 states it; byte-identical dupe cleanup stays a storage-layer property outside the engine. The record authorizes no implementation by itself; implementation is a separate packet when the atlas program prioritizes it. Closes #6041. --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? items.title: docs(atlas): staging-shard ingest gate design (#6057)
items.body: Design record for #6057 (Follow-up 38, Cluster 7; parent #6018). ## What this adds `doc/2026-11-08T13-45-00Z_design_atlas_staging_shard_ingest_gate/` — the gate design the issue asks for: - **Stage contracts for all five stages** (write, classify, dedup, provenance-check, publish), each as a pure function of the batch returning `(verdict, reason_codes, counts, artifacts)`. - **Per-stage pass/fail semantics** in one table (§4), including what `skip` means (never a pass, never bumps a snapshot id) and the fail-closed rule that no verdict = not passed. - **Failure/quarantine handling** (§5): quarantine is a state not a deletion; retry resumes at the failing stage; landing is content-addressed so retry is safe; long-lived epic units promote in increments; three-strikes escalation to stop auto-retrying a deterministic failure (spend guardrail, #6018 S3). - **Publish atomicity against fan-out search** (§6): the reader-visible invariant, the per-snapshot visibility contract, and the honest position that the indefinite Durable Object cache (#6788) is a known staleness window until #6805 lands rather than something the gate can claim atomic. ## Packet staleness handled The packet names #5755 as an open atomicity constraint. #5755 is **CLOSED (2026-11-07)**; its surface moved to #6662/#6664/#6665/#6666 and successor #6788 (+ eviction follow-up #6805). §6 addresses atomicity against those successors, not the closed issue. ## Sibling decisions consumed, not re-decided #6026 (versioning — landed design), #3125 (keep-all, occurrences), #5733 (dedup findings are data), #5669 (staging tier, ≤500-row bound, merge-on-close). The three obligations this note adds that those designs did not state (per-row tier split at publish, snapshot-id-in-manifest, three-strikes quarantine bound) are called out explicitly in §7 as gate requirements to reflect back, not as changes to their decisions. ## Follow-ons §9 splits implementation into six follow-ons. The gate-record state machine is tracked as #7709 against #5669; remaining follow-ons are filed against their siblings as those designs land. Design only — no implementation. Refs #6057 --- Open in [code]smith · Need help on this PR? Tag @codesmith-bot with what you need.

Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) to 7.30.2 and updates ancestor dependency [wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/wrangler). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.2

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 7.30.1 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

In Undici 7.x, the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

Undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] fix(decompress): join a repeated content-encoding header (#5664) by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6026
  • ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6087
  • fix(h1): backport ignore type of service errors to v7.x (#5547) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6076
  • [Backport v7.x] extractBody fixes 2 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#6093

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.30.1...v7.30.2

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

Updates `wrangler` from 4.147.0 to 4.166.0
Release notes

Sourced from wrangler's releases.

wrangler@4.166.0

Minor Changes

  • #16961 bf7568a Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Show configured trigger targets during experimental wrangler triggers deploy --dry-run

    Dry runs now print a "Would deploy" summary of routes, custom domains, cron schedules, Queue producers and consumers, Workflows, event triggers, and Email Routing addresses instead of exiting without a summary. Explicitly empty cron schedules and Email Routing addresses are shown as removals. The preview makes no API requests or authentication checks; when workers.dev is enabled, it reports that setting without looking up the account's subdomain.

  • #16679 be6aa81 Thanks @​mglewis! - Add images.url_transformations to the Wrangler configuration

    The images block now accepts a url_transformations object for controlling /cdn-cgi/image/ transformations on requests served by a Worker. enabled is required, and allowed_origins optionally lists the origins images may be fetched from (use ["*"] to allow any origin). binding is now optional, so url_transformations can be configured without an Images binding:

    {
  "images": {
    "url_transformations": {
      "enabled": true,
      "allowed_origins": ["images.example.com"]
    }
  }
}

    Like the rest of the images block, url_transformations is not inherited by named environments, and must be specified in each environment that needs it.

    cloudflare.config.ts gains the equivalent setting as a top-level images field on the Worker, with the Images binding remaining in env:

    export default defineConfig({
  worker: {
    name: "my-worker",
    compatibilityDate: "2026-11-01",
    images: {
      urlTransformations: {
        enabled: true,
        allowedOrigins: ["images.example.com"],
      },
    },
  },
});

    cf migrate carries images.url_transformations over to this field.

    This change adds configuration and validation only. url_transformations is not supported in previews.

  • #14114 dce615c Thanks @​dario-piotrowicz! - Add --show-diff flag to wrangler triggers deploy

    When --show-diff is passed, the command fetches the currently deployed trigger configuration from the remote worker and displays a colored diff against the local configuration before deploying. This covers routes, custom domains, cron schedules, and the workers_dev/preview_urls subdomain settings. Route and custom-domain lists are fetched only when that category has local entries to deploy, avoiding unnecessary permission requirements. Queue consumers and event triggers are not compared.

    The flag also works with --dry-run to preview these changes without actually deploying. Displaying a diff requires authentication, including during a dry run.

Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) to 7.30.2 and updates ancestor dependencies [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici), [cf](https://github.com/cloudflare/cf/tree/HEAD/packages/cli) and [wrangler](https://github.com/cloudflare/workers-sdk/tree/HEAD/packages/wrangler). These dependencies need to be updated together. Updates `undici` from 7.29.1 to 7.30.2
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v7.30.2

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 7.30.1 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

In Undici 7.x, the redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

In Undici 7.x, a downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

Undici 7.15.0 through 7.30.1 could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

What's Changed

  • [v7.x] fix(decompress): join a repeated content-encoding header (#5664) by @​mrityunjay-pandey in nodejs/undici#6026
  • ci: fix macOS WPT (Python 3.15) and job timeout on v7.x by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6087
  • fix(h1): backport ignore type of service errors to v7.x (#5547) by @​mcollina in nodejs/undici#6076
  • [Backport v7.x] extractBody fixes 2 by @​github-actions[bot] in nodejs/undici#6093

Full Changelog: https://github.com/nodejs/undici/compare/v7.30.1...v7.30.2

v7.30.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

... (truncated)
